description: We are a team of friends passionate about space and technology. Our crew includes programmers, designers, and space enthusiasts united by our love for exploring the universe. We combine technical skills with creative vision, including aspiring astrophysicists ready to reach for the stars!
summary:
Our project is an interactive dashboard with information about combustion experiments in microgravity and their results. It is designed for spacecraft crews, engineers, and researchers who need quick access to reliable data on fire behavior, material flammability, and fire suppression methods in space.
In microgravity, flames behave differently than on Earth: their shape, spread rate, temperature, smoke production, and the effectiveness of fire-suppression methods all change. Therefore, the results of ground-based tests cannot be directly applied to space conditions. NASA conducts such research to improve the safety of crews, equipment, and spacecraft.
The dashboard will bring together official NASA data on experiments, including SoFIE — research on the flammability of solid materials aboard the ISS — and Saffire — tests of the spread of larger fires aboard uncrewed Cygnus spacecraft. Users will be able to explore experimental conditions, materials used, observed effects, and practical conclusions for fire prevention.
The main goal of the project is to help avoid repeating past mistakes and make safer decisions when selecting materials, ventilation, fire-detection systems, and fire-suppression methods. This is especially important for long-duration missions, where quick access to verified knowledge can protect human lives and preserve the spacecraft
details: What it is and how it works: It's a user-friendly dashboard (a web panel) that shows how fire burns in space (under microgravity conditions on the ISS). In zero gravity, flames behave completely differently than on Earth—they are spherical and blue. Our program collects experimental data and visually displays it through charts and 3D models. What benefits and impact it has: Scientists no longer need to spend hours digging through boring spreadsheets. The platform helps them quickly see how fire spreads without Earth's gravity, which is crucial for the safety of future spacecraft. What we built it with: We used Python for calculations, React for an intuitive interface, and modern libraries for sleek 3D graphics. What makes it unique (creativity): We combined complex space physics with a simple, visually appealing, and interactive interface that is genuinely enjoyable to use. What the team considered: We focused on making the software fast so it can easily handle massive amounts of data without lagging.
